audit.report: Checkout degraded after a blocker restarted mid-negotiation, leaving pid 110239 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) idle in transaction and blocking sessions. Checkout success fell to 59% over 30s versus the 95% SLO, putting about $7,596/min of checkout revenue at risk and exceeding the business's 60s degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the replayable inventory_reconcile job, which the Continuity Guardian accepted because waiting would cost roughly $113,439 while a replay takes only 4 minutes. The independent authority initially denied the stale contract after the blocker reconnected as pid 110239, but re-authorized after re-observation. The executor terminated pid 110239 and verification confirmed recovery: 36/36 checkouts succeeded over 10s (100%), no lock waits remain, and no protected settlements were aborted.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 110239) held an idle open transaction that blocked checkout sessions, and its restart invalidated the first recovery contract.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile), capture the blocker PID and lock-graph state before proposing termination so a mid-negotiation restart does not stale the contract and force a renegotiation round.
audit.negotiation_critique: The guardians did not waste a round; both proposals were accepted in one round each, and all evidence (lock waits, checkout SLO, replayability, protected settlements, change calendar) was checked. The only override was the authority's invariant on live_identity, which correctly denied the stale v1 contract after the blocker reconnected as a new PID.
follow_ups: Confirm inventory_reconcile resumed from its last checkpoint and completed its 4-minute replay without blocking checkout.
Add an alert for batch_worker idle-in-transaction exceeding 5s on batch_replayable_inventory so the next blocker is caught before checkout falls below SLO.
